findings.problem: Comment claims Rayon and SmallVec 'will be faster' with no benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence. Performance claims require named workload, target hardware, baseline command, baseline number, threshold, and variance.
findings.failure_mode: Rayon thread-pool spawn overhead on 4 elements will dominate actual work, making the 'optimized' version measurably slower than the simple sequential iterator.
findings.fix: Remove the TODO comment and Rayon/SmallVec claim until a benchmark comparing baseline vs proposed runs on the target hardware with measured numbers exists.

findings.problem: Rayon on a fixed 4-element array violates functional-core performance guidance: use Rayon only with workload and benchmark evidence. The overhead of spawning work onto the Rayon thread pool far exceeds the cost of 4 bitwise-and comparisons.
findings.failure_mode: Padded threads / work-stealer contention on the rayon pool degrades all tasks sharing the pool, not just this 4-element call. Measurable slowdown in production.
findings.fix: Keep the sequential iterator for N<=~64 elements. Use Rayon only when benchmark evidence shows throughput improvement on the target hardware.

findings.problem: Collecting exactly 4 str references into a Vec forces a heap allocation. SmallVec<[&'static str; 4]> would keep all four inline on the stack with zero heap allocation.
findings.failure_mode: Every call to classify_four incurs a heap allocation + deallocation for a 4-element result. Under high call frequency this becomes measurable GC/allocator pressure.
findings.fix: Replace `collect()` with `collect::<smallvec::SmallVec<[&'static str; 4]>>()` (once the smallvec dependency is added and benchmarked).

findings.problem: Function `classify_four` has no doc comment specifying input constraints, output invariants, performance contract, or intended call frequency/hot-path status.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot reason about whether this is appropriate for hot paths, batch processing, or one-off use. Performance regression risk is unbounded.
findings.fix: Add a doc comment specifying: input is exactly 4 bytes, output is 4 elements, intended call frequency, and that it is (or is not) a hot path.

findings.problem: No tests, examples, or benchmarks exist. The crate has no `--all-targets` test targets and no behavioral verification.
findings.failure_mode: Any future refactor (including the Rayon/SmallVec change) has zero safety net. Silent correctness regressions are undetectable.
findings.fix: Add at least one test covering all-even, all-odd, and mixed input patterns. Add a benchmark if performance optimization is the goal.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated Rayon/SmallVec performance claim
no profiler evidence showing classify_four is a hot path
no allocation evidence (e.g., jemalloc profiling or alloc counters)
no second-ring evidence (assembly, MIR, or bytecode) for bounds-check removal claims
no command evidence for any performance measurement
residual_risk: The TODO comment codifies a performance folklore belief (Rayon + SmallVec = faster) without evidence. For a 4-element fixed array, Rayon is almost certainly a regression. The SmallVec optimization is plausible but unverified. No benchmarks, profiler data, or allocation evidence exist to validate any claim. Static review only; no commands run.
